deepDives.badge: DEEP DIVE #01 // SUPPLY CHAIN & DEV ENVIRONMENT
deepDives.title: Trojanized Claude Code Extension on Cursor Marketplace Deploys Persistent SSH Backdoor
deepDives.whatHappened: Threat actors successfully compromised developer publishing credentials on the Cursor Marketplace to release version 2.1.313 of the official Anthropic Claude Code extension. The malicious version weaponized developer installations by installing a stealthy persistent SSH backdoor, establishing reverse tunnels from internal corporate engineering networks directly to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
deepDives.technicalMechanism: Upon execution during IDE initialization, an obfuscated post-install JavaScript hook dynamically decoded a payload that invoked system shell commands. It read local public identity keys, injected an attacker-controlled ED25519 public key into the active user's `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`, altered `/etc/ssh/sshd_config` (or activated an embedded user-space SSH server if permissions were restricted), and beaconed the system's external IP, username, and local interface subnet topology to a command-and-control endpoint over HTTPS port 443.
deepDives.asciiFlow: [Cursor Marketplace: Compromised Publisher] ──► [v2.1.313 Auto-Update via IDE] ──► [Executes Post-Install Hook] ──► [Injects SSH Key into ~/.ssh/authorized_keys] ──► [Reverse Shell to C2]
remediation: Audit all developer workstations running Cursor or VS Code derivatives for the Claude Code extension version 2.1.313; remove immediately and wipe IDE extension directories.

Inspect and sanitize user and root `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` across all developer endpoints; revoke and rotate all enterprise SSH host keys and personal keypairs generated or stored on impacted endpoints.
Enforce enterprise MDM/EDR policies restricting IDE extension installation strictly to vetted internal private mirrors requiring manual hash verification and multi-maintainer approvals.
deepDives.lessonsLearned: Developer environments represent zero-trust boundary failures when third-party extension ecosystems operate with full user privilege. Organizations must treat IDE plugins as untrusted binaries, enforce software bill of materials (SBOM) scanning on development extensions, and execute AI agent plugins strictly within isolated sandboxes or containerized development environments.

deepDives.title: CVE-2026-97229: Maximum Severity Integer Overflow in GitLab CE/EE Exploited In The Wild
deepDives.whatHappened: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added CVE-2026-97229 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog following widespread telemetry showing automated threat actors weaponizing a maximum-severity integer overflow in GitLab Community and Enterprise Editions to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution on production source code repositories.
deepDives.technicalMechanism: The vulnerability resides in the backend repository object parsing and serialization routine when handling maliciously crafted archive streams or packfiles. By supplying an overly large chunk size parameter in a Git HTTP transport negotiation request, an attacker triggers an integer wrap during buffer size allocation. This leads to an undersized heap allocation followed by an unchecked memcpy, causing heap corruption that overwrites function pointer tables within the worker process, yielding arbitrary code execution under the privileges of the `git` user.
deepDives.asciiFlow: [Remote Attacker] ──► [HTTP POST /git-upload-pack with Malicious Packfile] ──► [Integer Wrap in Buffer Calculation] ──► [Heap Overflow & Memory Corruption] ──► [Root/Git Shell Execution]
remediation: Apply GitLab emergency security update immediately across all self-hosted Community Edition and Enterprise Edition instances.
Restrict access to self-hosted GitLab web and API interfaces using zero-trust network access (ZTNA) or VPN tunnels, removing public internet exposure.
Monitor GitLab host system logs and auditd for unexpected spawned child processes from the `git` or `gitlab-www` service accounts (e.g., execution of `/bin/sh`, `/bin/bash`, `curl`, or `wget`).
deepDives.lessonsLearned: Source code management systems are tier-0 assets containing the crown jewels of enterprise intellectual property and deployment pipelines. Exposing SCM web interfaces directly to the public internet without an application-aware identity reverse proxy exposes the organization to catastrophic supply chain takeover upon day-zero disclosure.

deepDives.badge: DEEP DIVE #03 // HARDWARE INTERDICTION & SUPPLY CHAIN
deepDives.title: Physical Supply Chain Interdiction: Cellular Hardware Implant Discovered in Trezor Safe 5
deepDives.whatHappened: A critical hardware supply chain interdiction incident was uncovered involving Trezor Safe 5 hardware wallets distributed by third-party reseller CryptoBilis. Devices were surgically modified prior to retail delivery with an unauthorized hardware daughterboard designed to secretly capture and transmit the user's master recovery seed over cellular bands during wallet initialization.
deepDives.technicalMechanism: Threat actors intercepted packaging downstream of original manufacturing, disassembling the ultrasonic-welded casing of the Trezor Safe 5. A micro-daughterboard featuring an eSIM-enabled GSM radio was micro-soldered directly to the internal I2C and SPI buses connecting the secure microcontroller to the touchscreen display. When the victim generates a new mnemonic seed phrase, the implant intercepts the unencrypted serial bus traffic directly off the display traces, formats the 12/24-word recovery phrase, and transmits it via SMS/cellular data to a foreign command server.
deepDives.asciiFlow: [User Initializes Wallet] ──► [Touchscreen SPI/I2C Displays Seed] ──► [Physical Implant Sniffs Bus] ──► [GSM Radio Exfiltrates Seed via Cellular] ──► [Attacker Drains Crypto Vault]
remediation: Issue mandatory security bulletins to all personnel and customers instructing anyone who purchased Trezor devices from CryptoBilis since March 2026 to immediately cease usage.
Perform immediate hot-to-cold asset migration: establish a new wallet on an authentic, factory-direct hardware unit using a newly generated seed phrase and transfer all balances immediately.

Establish hardware custody verification controls: mandate that cryptographic key generation devices must only be sourced directly from the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) with verifiable anti-tamper optical packaging.
deepDives.lessonsLearned: Zero-trust principles must extend to physical hardware acquisition. Critical security appliances and cryptographic signing devices sourced via third-party resellers or intermediaries carry intolerable supply chain risks. Organizations must enforce strict vendor pedigree, anti-tamper physical inspections, and independent bus-level hardware integrity audits.

dailyQuestions.scenario: A security operations analyst investigates an incident where an external attacker exploited an integer overflow vulnerability (CVE-2026-97229) in an internet-facing source code management server, achieving unauthenticated remote code execution. Which of the following compensating controls would have BEST mitigated the immediate impact before an official software patch was available?
options: A) Implementing disk-level full encryption on the database volume hosting repository metadata.
B) Placing the application behind a Web Application Firewall (WAF) configured with strict packet inspection and restricting administrative ingress to authorized VPN/ZTNA endpoints.
C) Changing the repository SSH access protocol from RSA-2048 to ED25519.
D) Enabling DNSSEC across the enterprise authoritative domain nameservers.
dailyQuestions.rationale: Placing the vulnerable application behind a Web Application Firewall (WAF) capable of deep payload inspection to filter malformed packfile requests, combined with restricting network ingress via Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) or VPN, isolates the vulnerable endpoint from unauthenticated internet-based exploitation. Full-disk encryption protects data at rest against physical theft, updating SSH key algorithms does not prevent HTTP transport layer exploitation, and DNSSEC only guarantees DNS response integrity.

dailyQuestions.scenario: Following the discovery of a rogue cellular daughterboard physically implanted into hardware wallets within an authorized reseller's distribution chain, a Principal Security Architect is tasked with overhauling the enterprise cryptographic key generation and cold storage architecture. Which of the following architectural strategies provides the STRONGEST defense-in-depth against hardware interdiction and physical bus-sniffing attacks?
options: A) Procuring cryptographic hardware exclusively from commercial secondary marketplaces that provide certificate of authenticity (CoA) stickers.

B) Implementing air-gapped, multi-vendor Shamir's Secret Sharing (SSS) or Multi-Party Computation (MPC) where key shares are generated on independently verified, diverse hardware platforms sourced strictly via direct OEM custody chains with tamper-evident packaging.
C) Enforcing full-disk bitlocker encryption on all engineer workstations that interface with hardware signing tokens over USB.
D) Requiring dual-custody passwords for accessing the enterprise password vault containing the hardware wallet mnemonic passphrases.
dailyQuestions.rationale: To defeat physical supply chain interdiction and bus-sniffing attacks, the architecture must eliminate single points of physical failure. Employing multi-party computation (MPC) or Shamir's Secret Sharing (SSS) across heterogeneous, independently audited hardware sourced strictly via verified OEM direct custody chains guarantees that a compromise of any single vendor's device or supply chain will not result in the exfiltration or compromise of the master key. Secondary marketplaces heighten interdiction risk, workstation disk encryption does not protect external hardware buses, and storing mnemonic seeds in a shared password vault completely undermines hardware-isolated key generation.

detectionRules.code:
title: Suspicious Modification of SSH Authorized Keys by IDE Subprocess
id: 9b2d8e41-01f4-4a27-a63e-72bc38f2190a
status: production
description: Detects IDE execution contexts (Cursor, Code, VSCode) spawning shell or script interpreters that append or overwrite SSH authorized_keys files, characteristic of trojanized marketplace extensions.

  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/official-claude-code-vs-code-extension.html
author: Global Intel Hub Engineering
date: 2026-10-30
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/cursor'
      - '/code'
      - '/electron'
      - '/node'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '.ssh/authorized_keys'
      - 'authorized_keys'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child
fields:
  - Image
  - CommandLine
  - ParentImage
  - ParentCommandLine
  - User
